manuscript.title: Metabolomic markers of sleep disruption in shift workers

evidenceCorpus.title: Abstract objective
evidenceCorpus.excerpt: We evaluated whether plasma metabolomic profiles differed between night-shift and day-shift hospital staff.

evidenceCorpus.title: Methods
evidenceCorpus.excerpt: The cohort included 184 participants with repeated fasting plasma samples and actigraphy-derived sleep measures.

evidenceCorpus.title: Results
evidenceCorpus.excerpt: Night-shift workers showed higher kynurenine and lower phosphatidylcholine levels after adjustment for age, sex, caffeine intake, and body mass index.

evidenceCorpus.title: Statistical notes
evidenceCorpus.excerpt: The draft describes p = 0.08 as significant for the exploratory lipid panel and omits confidence intervals for the adjusted odds ratio.

evidenceCorpus.title: Kynurenine pathway changes in circadian disruption
evidenceCorpus.excerpt: Prior work links circadian disruption with kynurenine pathway remodeling and inflammatory signaling.

claims.text: Night-shift work is associated with higher kynurenine concentrations.
Sleep disruption causes the observed phosphatidylcholine decrease.

summaries.text: Objective: evaluate plasma metabolomic profiles in night-shift and day-shift hospital staff. Methods: 184 participants provided repeated fasting plasma samples with actigraphy-derived sleep measures. Results: night-shift workers showed higher kynurenine and lower phosphatidylcholine after adjustment. Conclusion: the data support a metabolomic association with shift work, but causal sleep claims need stronger evidence.
implications: Metabolomic screening may help prioritize follow-up studies
nextSteps: Add confidence intervals and avoid causal wording

summaries.text: This paper says night-shift hospital staff had metabolomic perturbations in kynurenine and phosphatidylcholine.
keyFindings: Night-shift workers had different blood chemistry
implications: Work schedules may be linked with health-related chemistry changes
nextSteps: Explain the result with simpler words
